title: Transliteration of the Voynich MS text
summary: Zandbergen documents five major transliterations and compares them using a common format and a superset alphabet. The paper also measures how different choices about uncertain spaces affect token counts and singleton types.
established: Under the common symbol comparison in Table 7, four files generally agree above 95 percent. The Glen Claston file agrees at approximately 90.5–92.0 percent for exact symbols, while its family-level agreement with Zandbergen–Landini is 99.0 percent.

Table 6 reports different locus coverage across the five files. The hapax comparison therefore restricts attention to three comparably complete files and treats uncertain separators separately where the source marks them.

open.question: Which fine-grained glyph distinctions recorded in v101 are reproducible across scribal hands when assessed directly against the manuscript images?
open.check: Select matched instances of the disputed glyph families and have independent reviewers annotate image crops blind to the transliteration. Report agreement at both the family and variant levels.
